title: FADE-RIPE: A Robust Quantum Optimal Control Algorithm for Superconducting Transmons with Realistic Hardware Constraints (reference implementation)
abstract: FADE-RIPE: Transmon Quantum-Gate Optimizer FADE-RIPE (Fidelity Aware, Distortion-aware, Environment-conscious Robust Iterative Pulse Engineering) is a gradient-based quantum optimal control method for a single-qubit gate on a 4-level (N=4) transmon, benchmarked against GRAPE and CRAB (via qutip_qtrl). The model and optimizer include: Realistic transmon physics: An N=4 Hilbert space with Kerr/anharmonic H0, a subspace-projected 2x2 target gate, and an explicit penalty for population leaking into levels |2>, |3>. Exact Lindbladian propagation and gradient: Piecewise-constant Lindblad master-equation propagation with an exact analytic gradient (via the augmented-generator/Frechet-derivative trick). AWG bandwidth filter: A Butterworth low-pass filter on the control pulses, represented as an exact linear operator so the gradient chain rule through it is exact. Filter-function noise penalty: A numerical filter function F(omega) of the optimized pulse, penalized against a 1/f (flux) or thermal-photon power spectral density via an overlap integral. Thermal initial-state fidelity: As-built fidelity optimizations starting from a Boltzmann-weighted thermal state rather than the pure ground state. This upload contains the reference implementation fade_realistic.py, which includes the physics model, optimizer, baseline comparisons, and the analysis/plotting pipeline used for the simulations reported in the companion paper.

title: Core Claim: Design a dynamic adjustment algorithm for quantum entanglement-based hidden variables, leveraging the unique properties of hidden variables to achieve automatic data distribution learning and modeling, and enhance algorithm robustness.
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a potential paradigm shift in data analysis, offering capabilities exceeding classical methods. This research explores the application of dynamic adjustment algorithms for quantum entanglement-based hidden variables. The core idea revolves around utilizing the inherent properties of hidden variables – their capacity to influence data distribution – to automate the learning and modeling process. The presented algorithm employs an adaptive approach, dynamically adjusting parameters to optimize data distribution based on observed patterns. This approach contrasts with traditional methods that rely on pre-defined parameters, promising enhanced robustness and adaptability. The study investigates the potential of this dynamic adjustment to improve the performance of quantum entanglement-based algorithms across diverse data distributions. The implementation focuses on optimizing a specific metric – data fidelity – by iteratively refining the algorithm's parameters. This research aims to establish a foundational framework for harnessing the power of hidden variables to achieve more efficient and reliable data analysis in the quantum realm.

title: Decentralized Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Consensus-Based Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility and design of decentralized learning systems capable of Byzantine fault tolerance. The core challenge lies in training neural networks across a distributed network where some nodes may be compromised and actively attempting to disrupt the learning process – a scenario known as Byzantine fault tolerance. We propose a consensus-based neural network training algorithm that leverages a voting mechanism to achieve agreement on model parameters despite the presence of malicious actors. This approach allows for robust learning even when a significant portion of the network is corrupted. The system is designed to tolerate a certain level of Byzantine failures without compromising the accuracy or convergence of the trained model. We formalize the algorithm using mathematical notation and demonstrate its theoretical properties, focusing on convergence and fault tolerance. The key contributions of this work are the detailed specification of the consensus protocol and its integration with a distributed neural network training process.

title: Probability Form Semantic Networks (PFSSNs)
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Form Semantic Networks (PFSSNs), a novel approach to semantic network representation and reasoning. The core claim is that semantic network nodes and edges should no longer be treated as discrete values, but rather as probability distributions, representing the fuzzy associations between concepts. This work leverages Bayesian networks as the underlying mechanism to model these relationships, enabling probabilistic inference and effectively handling the inherent uncertainty in semantic data. PFSSNs provide a more robust and flexible framework for semantic reasoning compared to traditional semantic networks that rely on discrete representations. The proposed method addresses the limitations of existing approaches by incorporating probabilistic modeling, allowing for a nuanced understanding of concept interrelationships and facilitating more accurate and reliable semantic inference. This work demonstrates the potential of PFSSNs for applications requiring robust reasoning under conditions of uncertainty.

title: Automated Theorem Proving for Hardware Security Protocols
abstract: This paper explores the application of automated theorem proving (ATP) to the rigorous verification of hardware security protocols. Current security verification methods often rely on manual analysis, which is prone to human error and struggles to scale with increasingly complex protocols. We propose a novel approach that leverages ATP systems to formally model and verify the correctness of these protocols. The core mechanism involves translating protocol specifications into formal logic statements and then employing an ATP engine to automatically deduce whether the protocol satisfies its intended security properties. This approach offers a reliable, scalable, and potentially more exhaustive method for identifying vulnerabilities compared to traditional approaches. We outline the key steps involved, highlighting the challenges and potential benefits of this paradigm shift in hardware security verification. This work contributes to the development of more robust and trustworthy hardware security systems. ---

title: Emergent Code Generation and Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the concept of emergent code generation through the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms. The core idea is to leverage the principles of biological evolution to automatically produce code snippets with complex functionality and optimized performance. Unlike traditional code generation methods that rely on predefined rules or templates, this approach employs a dynamic process where code fragments are treated as 'genes' and subjected to evolutionary operations such as crossover and mutation. The resulting code evolves iteratively, guided by predefined performance metrics. We demonstrate a framework where code snippets are evaluated based on specified criteria, with fitter snippets being selected for reproduction and further modification. This process facilitates the discovery of novel code structures and optimization strategies that might be difficult to conceive through conventional design methods. The key innovation lies in the ability to explore the vast design space of code solutions in a self-organizing manner, leading to emergent behaviors and solutions. The paper outlines the proposed methodology and highlights the potential of this approach for automating software development and optimization tasks.

title: Title: Spatiotemporal Quantum State Synchronization – Wavelet-Based Integration
abstract: Quantum communication relies heavily on the synchronization of quantum states across spatially separated devices. Current methods often struggle with achieving high fidelity and scalability due to complex measurement and synchronization requirements. This paper proposes a novel technique utilizing wavelet-based integration to efficiently synchronize quantum states across spatially separated devices, offering a significant advancement in fidelity and scalability. We introduce a framework where quantum states are integrated using wavelet transforms, allowing for more robust and adaptable synchronization protocols. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the wavelets' ability to represent complex patterns and efficiently manage the integration process. This approach promises improved fidelity and scalability compared to existing synchronization methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing its potential for enhancing the reliability of quantum communication systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE&D)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding and decoding, termed Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE&D), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that QIE&D offers a fundamentally new method for information processing, surpassing the limitations imposed by classical information theory. The underlying mechanism utilizes multi-particle entanglement to construct an encoder-decoder system. The encoding process maps information onto entangled states across multiple quantum particles, while the decoding process extracts the original information through measurements on these entangled states, enhanced by entanglement transformations to improve robustness against noise. QIE&D distinguishes itself from existing quantum information processing techniques by employing multi-body entanglement, providing significantly greater information capacity and processing power. This system is designed to address the challenges associated with long-distance quantum communication and secure quantum computation. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the key components and operational principles of the QIE&D system. We explore the mathematical formalism underpinning the encoding and decoding processes, focusing on the manipulation of entangled states and the application of entanglement transformations. Furthermore, we analyze the system's sensitivity to various types of noise and propose strategies for mitigating these effects. The potential of QIE&D is significant, offering a pathway toward more efficient and secure information transmission and processing in the quantum realm.

title: Co-Evolving Structured Knowledge and Reasoning in Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-augmented methods improve factual accuracy by grounding language models in external knowledge, but retrieving over unstructured text often introduces irrelevant context and offers limited control over the retrieved information. Structured knowledge bases offer a more controllable alternative, yet they are expensive to construct and often brittle to reason over. To address these limitations, we propose KBevo: a co-evolving framework that jointly learns to construct a structured knowledge base and reason over it for knowledge-intensive question answering. By optimizing both components end-to-end with QA outcome rewards, our method enables reasoning success to directly improve the quality of the constructed knowledge base. This leads to larger, better-connected knowledge structures with higher answer reachability, while also improving compositional factual reasoning and controllability compared to standard retrieval baselines.

title: Multi-Campus Google Review Analytics Dataset and Reproducibility Package for Service Benchmarking, Domain Generalization, and Reviewer Graph Analysis
abstract: This record provides the processed datasets, supplementary materials, analysis code, frozen data partitions, per-review predictions, result tables, and reproducibility documentation supporting three complementary studies of multi-campus Google reviews. The studies address: (1) aspect-based sentiment analysis and rating–text consistency for cross-campus service benchmarking; (2) imbalanced multilingual sentiment classification under cross-campus domain generalization; and (3) reviewer–campus bipartite graph analysis and reviewer-aware rating aggregation. The frozen corpus contains 6,990 reviews collected from 13 predefined campus listings, including 2,932 reviews with textual content. The sentiment-analysis component includes a 1,200-review human-validated annotation set covering global text sentiment, rating–text consistency, aspect presence, and aspect-level sentiment across eleven service categories. The domain-generalization component provides leakage-controlled frozen partitions, campus-held-out evaluation outputs, and prediction records. The graph-analysis component contains 6,990 reviewer–campus edges, 6,363 pseudonymous reviewer nodes, 13 campus nodes, and all 78 possible campus pairs. Reviewer identities are pseudonymized, and direct profile identifiers and profile images are excluded from the research package. The three analytical tracks are maintained separately to preserve their distinct research questions, units of analysis, and experimental outputs. The package includes documentation describing data provenance, processing decisions, annotation structure, analytical limitations, and reproducibility procedures. This release is version 1.0.0.

title: Field-Adaptive Geometry and Arithmetic Methods – Through Dynamic Learning of Field Features, Automated Construction and Optimization of Geometric-Arithmetic Models
abstract: Field-adaptive geometry and arithmetic methods offer a paradigm shift in modeling, enabling automated construction and optimization of geometric-arithmetic models tailored to specific field characteristics. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging dynamic learning of field features to automatically adjust model parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and generalization capabilities. We propose a new algorithm for learning and adapting these models based on data patterns. The core mechanism centers on a field feature learning algorithm that iteratively adjusts the model's parameters to optimally fit the input data. This results in a more flexible and robust system compared to static, fixed models. The work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on diverse geometric and arithmetic datasets, showcasing its ability to achieve state-of-the-art performance.

title: 基于自适应的量子算法优化策略
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm optimization strategy that leverages adaptive learning algorithms to dynamically adjust quantum algorithm parameters. Traditional approaches often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. Our method aims to improve quantum algorithm efficiency and accuracy by automatically optimizing these parameters based on the input data. We present a framework that incorporates a self-learning mechanism to adaptively adjust parameters, offering a significant improvement over existing methods. The core of our approach involves a dynamic parameter adjustment process guided by a learned model that constantly evaluates the algorithm's performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy through theoretical analysis and simulations, showcasing its potential to accelerate algorithm execution and enhance results.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Parameter Tuning
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to unlock unprecedented computational capabilities. This paper explores the potential of adaptive parameter tuning within QML models, a critical challenge in achieving optimal performance. We propose a novel mechanism that integrates quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust model parameters, responding to data distribution shifts. This approach surpasses traditional static parameter optimization techniques, offering a more robust and adaptable learning process. The study details the theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this adaptive tuning strategy in a specific QML model. The focus is on enhancing model generalization and robustness.

abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology to enhance the adaptability and predictive capabilities of complex topological models. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that adjusts topology based on observed data, driving a continuous refinement of the model's representation.

title: Title: Algorithmic Resonance-Based Quantum Simulation (ARQS)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Resonance-Based Quantum Simulation (ARQS), a novel quantum simulation algorithm designed to dramatically enhance the fidelity of quantum system simulations through the utilization of resonant frequencies. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with accuracy, particularly for complex systems due to the inherent challenges of representing and manipulating quantum states. ARQS addresses these challenges by exploiting the inherent resonance properties of quantum systems to dynamically adjust simulation parameters, effectively reducing computational cost and error. The core mechanism of ARQS involves identifying resonant frequencies within the system and utilizing them to 'tune' the simulation, leading to a significant improvement in simulation fidelity. This research explores the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results supporting the potential of ARQS to revolutionize quantum science.

title: 基于自律的量子计算的熵特征优化
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm in computation, relies heavily on the stability and reliability of its quantum bits (qubits). Qubit errors are a significant challenge, threatening the accuracy of quantum computations. title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed routing protocol for quantum networks leveraging the topological properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to construct a network topology based on entangled states between nodes, enabling communication through the instantaneous correlation inherent in entanglement. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional routing protocols, particularly in terms of speed and security. We define a routing algorithm that dynamically adjusts the entanglement states to facilitate data transmission, effectively creating a network with inherently high bandwidth and resilience to eavesdropping. The algorithm is based on a graph theory framework where nodes represent quantum devices and edges represent entangled pairs. The routing process involves identifying the shortest path through the entanglement network, leveraging the correlated states for rapid information transfer. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of this protocol, outlining key formulas for calculating entanglement metrics, path distances, and routing decisions. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research and development in quantum network architecture and routing strategies.

title: Cognitive Landscape Modeling (CLM)
abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Landscape Modeling (CLM), a novel system for modeling the emergent cognitive landscapes of complex systems. The core claim is that CLM dynamically adjusts the relative importance of different cognitive processes based on environmental input, creating a 'landscape' representation of a system's cognitive activity. We leverage Bayesian inference and agent-based modeling to construct this landscape, enabling a dynamic adaptation of task allocation. CLM offers a departure from traditional cognitive models by focusing on the emergent properties of these cognitive landscapes, providing a more holistic understanding of complex behavior.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection in Complex Systems
abstract: Anomaly detection in complex systems presents significant challenges due to the inherent complexity, high dimensionality, and often unknown nature of system dynamics. Traditional methods frequently rely on reactive pattern matching, which can be easily overwhelmed by noise and fail to capture underlying causal relationships. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to enhance anomaly detection capabilities. The core idea is to model the system's dependencies and dynamics explicitly using a CBN. Observed data is then used to infer the probability of different system states, allowing us to identify anomalies as deviations from the expected behavior based on the learned causal structure. This approach offers a proactive and robust method for anomaly detection, significantly improving upon the limitations of traditional reactive techniques. The proposed method leverages Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty and provides a framework for understanding the root causes of anomalies, not just their presence.

title: Rule-based semantic hypergraph parsing from textual annotations
abstract: A semantic hypergraph is a knowledge representation capable of capturing the hierarchical and multi-relational structures essential in natural language. This paper introduces a rule-based semantic hypergraph parser that transforms textual annotations (dependency trees, semantic roles, coreferences) into a semantic hypergraph. The semantic hypergraph parser preserves nested semantic relationships through recursive and ordered hyperedges, integrating predicate-argument structures and coreferences directly into its hypergraph structure. The input textual annotations, the resulting semantic hypergraph representation, and the rule-based transformations applied during parsing are described in detail. The semantic hypergraph parser is evaluated against an existing parser. The qualitative comparison revealed our parser's strengths in handling adverbial modifiers, adjectival clauses, and coreferences. Quantitative evaluation was performed on two datasets: a large-scale corpus of annotated natural language texts, and a manually curated dataset with gold-standard hypergraph annotations. The results show that our parser output achieves almost perfect alignment with gold annotations, outperforming the existing parser by 3–18% on nested representations. After eliminating baseline differences, statistical significance testing confirmed that these improvements were robust across syntactic constructions. We have publicly released our parser to support research on structured semantic representation and to enable practical artificial intelligence applications, including semantic parsing, text mining, and knowledge extraction.

title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?
abstract: When can an agent failure be caught? An audit is usually limited by the record rather than by the method. CatchBench therefore puts one auditor's question to three information states: the declared configuration before a run (PRE), a growing prefix of its trace (LIVE), and the finished trace (POST). Prior benchmarks fix one of these states or vary the telemetry; to our knowledge none scores all three under one task-method interface. Each state admits different questions, so seven task contracts carry their own labels and metrics rather than one leaderboard. Four are evidential; three are Gold-derived mechanism diagnostics. The release scores 72 entrants, from rule scanners and structural models to eleven LLM judges across nine model families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Gemma, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Nova), over 1187 declared configurations and 1162 recorded runs. Most of the arena does not order: 56 of 138 registered contrasts separate, and the rest are published unresolved rather than ranked. The two sharpest results cut against our own data. One rule ignores every name and permission; it flags each capability declared after the first. On one of six configuration sources it reaches a perfect F1, so a score there measures how the corpus was built rather than how well a method reasons. Our admissibility bar then rejected one injected substrate and withheld evidential status from the other. A benchmark number is therefore not interpretable until the process behind its labels is published and tested for the shortcut it may leave. We report both, and regenerate every ordering from released predictions with no model call.

title: Differential Candidate-Key Contraction in an Experimental GF(101)^4 Feistel Construction: An Empirical Study of Known and Unknown Difference Observations
abstract: We report an empirical phenomenon in which repeated differential observations of a small experimental Feistel construction over (GF(101)) progressively contract a finite population of candidate keys. The construction operates on four field elements using eight Feistel rounds. Four candidate round-function families are defined within the construction; two configurations, denoted (F_0) and (F_1), are examined in detail. Starting from a population of 100,000 candidate keys, known-difference observations reached the planted reference key within three to four observations in the tested experiments. When the input difference was not supplied to the candidate-filtering procedure, substantially more observations were required: in an extended experiment using (F_0), the planted key became unique after 30, 30, and 31 observations for three independent seeds. The (F_0) and (F_1) configurations exhibited similar contraction behavior in the tested experiments. With 20 unknown-difference observations, the numbers of surviving candidates were 31, 21, and 19 for (F_0), and 28, 16, and 30 for (F_1), across three seeds. A reproducibility audit was also performed on an earlier informal record of the experiment. That record reported 23 surviving candidates at observation 20 for one configuration. The current verified reconstruction produces 11 survivors under the same recorded experimental description. The candidate population was verified to be identical to the archived population by SHA-256 hash. An exhaustive local feasibility analysis further showed that 23 survivors cannot be obtained from the verified 29-candidate intermediate state under the verified filtering rule, regardless of which observation values are substituted for the next two observations. We document this discrepancy as a reproducibility issue rather than interpreting it as a cryptographic phenomenon. This report is intended as a dated and citable experimental record. It does not claim priority over the established literature on differential cryptanalysis or related cryptographic analysis techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Probability Distribution Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a probabilistic distribution model for quantum entanglement computation, leveraging the unique properties of entangled states. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the probability distribution based on the evolving state of entangled qubits, ultimately aiming to enhance the precision of quantum calculations. This research addresses a critical challenge in quantum computing: accurately predicting and controlling the complex evolution of entangled states. The core claim is that this model provides a pathway to more efficient and robust quantum computations through a deep understanding of entanglement dynamics.

title: Title: Bayesian Probability of Non-Linear Systems
abstract: This paper explores a novel Bayesian approach to estimating the probability of outcomes in complex, non-linear systems. Traditional methods often struggle with noise and uncertainty, rendering them inadequate for accurately assessing probabilities within these systems. This work proposes a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) framework that explicitly models the interactions between variables and their uncertainties, offering a more robust and adaptive probabilistic assessment. The core mechanism involves a shift away from simple mean-field estimation towards a dynamically updating model, addressing the limitations of existing techniques. This paper details the design, implementation, and evaluation of this new method, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the estimation of probabilities in challenging, non-linear scenarios.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Space Partitioning via Entanglement
abstract: Quantum state space partitioning is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, crucial for efficiently exploring complex quantum states. Current approaches often struggle with the exponential scaling of computational complexity, hindering practical applications. This paper introduces a novel technique – Non-Local Quantum State Space Partitioning via Entanglement – designed to overcome these limitations. We propose a quantum algorithm that leverages entanglement to create interconnected sub-spaces within the quantum state space, enabling parallel exploration and significantly accelerating the search for solutions. Entanglement is used to create a 'quantum mesh' – a structure where states are connected and interconnected, facilitating efficient traversal. This method offers a potentially revolutionary speedup compared to existing algorithms, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional quantum states. We detail the algorithm's core mechanisms, demonstrate its effectiveness through simplified examples, and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Quantum Link-Based Quantum State Transfer Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for instantaneous communication and information transfer. title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Optimization for Robotics
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-enhanced constraint optimization to robotics, specifically focusing on dynamic adjustment of robot control parameters to maximize task performance. abstract: This paper presents an innovative algorithm optimization framework leveraging adaptive topology structures. Traditional optimization methods primarily focus on parameter tuning, whereas this approach dynamically adjusts the topology of the algorithm to enhance performance. Through this dynamic transformation, we aim to reduce computational complexity and potentially unlock new optimization strategies. The core mechanism centers on the concept of topology as a structural constraint, allowing for intelligent adjustments that significantly impact algorithm efficiency. This work explores the potential of this adaptive approach to address challenges in various computational domains. The investigation will demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. This study seeks to advance the field of algorithm optimization by introducing a novel approach that adapts to the inherent properties of the algorithm itself.

title: Based on Simulated Evolution Algorithm for Hardware Design Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of Simulated Evolution Algorithms (SEA) to the optimization of hardware design. Traditional hardware design methodologies often rely heavily on manual intervention and iterative refinement, a process that can be time-consuming and potentially limit the exploration of the design space. This work proposes a novel approach where a SEA is leveraged to automatically generate hardware designs that meet specified functional and performance criteria. The core mechanism involves formulating the hardware design problem as a simulated evolutionary process. An SEA is used to produce design alternatives, which are then evaluated through simulation. The best-performing designs are selected as parents for subsequent generations, undergoing crossover and mutation operators to drive the evolution towards optimal solutions. The key benefit of this methodology is its ability to efficiently explore the design space and identify superior designs without significant manual intervention. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key stages and considerations for implementing an SEA-driven hardware design optimization process. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in hardware design, moving towards automated and intelligent design solutions.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Formal Model Verification
abstract: The increasing deployment of machine learning (ML) models in critical applications raises significant concerns regarding transparency and trustworthiness. Many ML models, particularly deep neural networks, operate as "black boxes," making it difficult to understand their internal decision-making processes. This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithmic transparency by leveraging formal model verification techniques. We argue that formal verification provides a rigorous method for establishing guarantees about the behavior of ML algorithms, moving beyond post-hoc explanations and offering verifiable proof of correctness. Specifically, we apply formal methods, such as model checking and theorem proving, to analyze ML algorithms. This process generates detailed proofs of correctness, identifies potential vulnerabilities, and ultimately enhances the trustworthiness of ML systems. The core claim is that formal model verification offers a robust solution to the black-box problem, providing a path towards more reliable and explainable AI. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, highlighting its importance in ensuring responsible AI development and deployment. ---

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Wavefunction Collapse Network (WECEN)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Wavefunction Collapse Network (WECN) presents a novel approach to quantum computation and simulation utilizing quantum entanglement to accelerate wavefunction collapse. The core concept hinges on establishing a network of entangled qubits, strategically positioned to facilitate rapid and controlled collapse events, thereby significantly boosting the speed and accuracy of calculations within complex systems. This research focuses on demonstrating the efficacy of this methodology through a series of simulations and preliminary experiments designed to illustrate the potential for quantum acceleration in quantum physics. This paper explores the theoretical underpinnings of WECN, details the implementation of the network architecture, and presents preliminary results showcasing the enhanced computational capabilities compared to classical methods. We investigate the impact of entanglement fidelity and network topology on collapse rates.

title: Quantum Topology Network Control Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology networks, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, offer unprecedented opportunities for secure communication and distributed quantum computing. This research investigates a novel control algorithm predicated on quantum entanglement and quantum gates, designed to dynamically manage and optimize the behavior of quantum network nodes. The core mechanism focuses on harnessing the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states to achieve precise control and robust network stability. Traditional control methods often struggle with dynamic environments, necessitating a fundamentally different approach. This algorithm addresses this challenge by employing quantum entanglement as a key resource for dynamic adjustment and feedback, leading to enhanced network performance and stability. The proposed algorithm offers a significant advancement in the control and management of quantum networks, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing and communication.

title: Domain-Adaptive Probability Model (DAPM) - Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces the Domain-Adaptive Probability Model (DAPM), a novel framework for probabilistic modeling that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on both input data and internal state dynamics. The core aim is to enhance model generalization and prediction accuracy by providing a mechanism to adapt to changing data distributions. We detail the DAPM's architecture, parameter adjustment strategy, and validation procedures. The paper demonstrates the efficacy of DAPM through comparative analysis with established probabilistic models, showcasing improved performance across diverse datasets. The significance of this work lies in its ability to provide a flexible and adaptive approach to probabilistic modeling, overcoming limitations of static parameterization.

title: Neural Network Connection Weight Dynamic Topology Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network training that dynamically optimizes the topology of connections between neurons. Traditional neural network training methods primarily focus on adjusting connection weights, often neglecting the inherent impact of the network's structure on performance. We propose a methodology employing an evolutionary algorithm, specifically a genetic algorithm, to iteratively refine the network's topology alongside its weights. The core idea is to treat the combination of connection weights and topology as a single optimization problem, enabling the algorithm to discover network structures that are significantly more efficient and effective than those produced by conventional training methods. The algorithm's adaptive nature allows it to respond to changing data distributions or task requirements, potentially leading to robust and adaptable neural networks. This work addresses the limitations of static network architectures by introducing a dynamic topology optimization process, ultimately aiming for improved accuracy, speed, and generalization capabilities.

title: Dynamic Code Generation through Genetic Grammars
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to software development—dynamic code generation—utilizing genetic grammars. The core concept involves evolving code structures through a genetic algorithm, guided by a fitness function that assesses code's adherence to desired functionality and constraints. This methodology aims to automate portions of the software development lifecycle, reducing manual effort and potentially leading to more efficient and optimized code. The system employs a genetic grammar, subject to mutation and crossover operations, to produce increasingly suitable code solutions. The paper outlines the fundamental principles, the mechanism of operation, and highlights the potential advantages of this dynamic generation approach compared to traditional coding methods.

The core mechanism involves a neural network that learns and adapts to the system's inherent complexity, resulting in improved performance across diverse scenarios. This work offers a significant advancement in complexity scaling techniques, promising increased accuracy and reduced reliance on manual tuning.

title: Gradient Boosting Machines (XGBoost, LightGBM) with Stacked Generalization for Multi‐Task Learning in Graph‐based Predictive Analytics
abstract: Multi-task learning has become one of the potent paradigms of enhancement of the generalization and sample efficiency that depends on the use of shared representations among various related learning objectives. This chapter introduces a new design to combine gradient boosting machines, namely, XGBoost and LightGBM applications, with stacked generalization models to solve the problem of multi-task learning. The five benchmark datasets were tested on the proposed approach and covers the variety of domains such as computer vision, natural language processing and structured data analysis. These datasets include: CIFAR-100 feature set, adult income census, multi-domain sentiment, MNIST variant tasks, and medical health records. The framework was developed to clearly model task relations as one learns task-specific decision limits and common feature depictions. By integrating predictive learning with adaptive optimization, the framework effectively addresses workload fluctuations and scalability challenges commonly encountered in cloud computing systems.

title: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end evaluation framework for image-triggered command injection against computer-use agents (CUAs). The goal is to test whether a local visual patch can induce verifiable environmental consequences along the full chain of screenshot input, VLM generation, action parsing, and environment execution. We train and deploy patches on author-controlled GitHub Pages pages and a locally deployed CSDN clone, and evaluate them in real environments across five open-source or publicly available GUI-agent or vision-language-model (VLM) backends. Our experiment aggregates 600 instance-level online cases, with T-ASR, TAPR, and E2E-ASR reaching 84.5%, 47.0%, and 20.3%, respectively. Trajectory analysis further shows that in some successful cases the agent first executes a malicious terminal command and then continues the original benign task. These results indicate that optimized local visual signals can affect not only VLM outputs but also propagate through the execution pipeline of open CUAs and create real environmental risk.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Learning Framework for Intelligent and AI-Native 6G Wireless Networks
abstract: The recent convergence of 6G wireless systems and Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) has driven the need for on-device intelligence in edge networks, where ultra-low latency, stringent energy budgets, and tight compute constraints demand novel architectures. Lightweight deep models efficiently extract local patterns but fail to capture global dependencies, while attention mechanisms do so at the expense of energy and computational cost. To bridge this gap, we introduce Quantumer, a hybrid TinyML--quantum framework that integrates multi-scale dilated convolutions and scaled dot-product attention within a lightweight transformer architecture, employing a two-stage transfer learning pipeline from Quantum Pre-Training (Quantumer-Q) to Classical Fine-Tuning (Quantumer-C). We also present QuantiblentLayer, a four-qubit variational circuit that maps compact traffic representations into measurement-based Hilbert-space features using trainable rotations and cyclic entangling operations. The circuit is used only during offline pre-training as a nonlinear embedding teacher and is removed before Quantumer-C deployment, leaving a fully classical inference model without runtime quantum execution. By transferring these quantum-assisted embeddings into an energy-efficient, lightweight transformer, Quantumer achieves strong detection performance with minimal compute and memory overhead on resource-constrained edge devices. The intrusion detection system (IDS) is used as a case study and evaluated on the Edge-IIoTset, TON IoT, and WUSTL-IIoT-2021 datasets. Quantumer-Q achieves competitive compact-model performance with 105.86K parameters, 0.4038 MB memory usage, 0.5525 MB model size, and 5.5646 MFLOPs; the INT8 Raspberry Pi 4 deployment obtains 16.8413 ms latency with a 0.6493 MB footprint. These results support training-time quantum-assisted representation learning for compact edge-deployable IDS.

title: Adaptive Bridge: A Proxy-Based Decoupling Layer for Mitigating DDS Backpressure in ROS 2
abstract: In systems built on Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) and using Data Distribution Service (DDS), a single network-impaired or throttled subscriber on a RELIABLE topic can cause backpressure that degrades throughput and latency for all other subscribers, including safety-critical ones sharing the publisher, because the publisher's DDS writer can no longer accept new samples. We present Adaptive Bridge, a proxy-based layer that decouples critical subscribers from degraded or noncritical ones, thereby isolating the critical path through topic splitting and dynamic rate control. The proxy acts as a middleman and subscribes to the original topic and republishes the messages to two independent DDS writers: one RELIABLE writer for critical nodes and one BEST EFFORT writer for noncritical or degraded nodes, thus isolating the degraded nodes and safeguarding the publisher and critical nodes from backpressure. A probe-based classifier actively monitors subscriber health through sampling with hysteresis and adjusts subscriber rate limits in real time. We evaluate the system under a Gilbert-Elliott bursty wireless loss model using a reproducible Docker-based harness. The results show that using the Adaptive Bridge in our evaluation harness reduces the critical subscriber tail p95 latency from up to 15 s to 1.55 ms across all impairment severities while preserving the publisher's configured throughput.

title: rcc-refcert: a Python research toolkit for structure-fair quantum circuit complexity
abstract: rcc-refcert is a Python research toolkit for structure-fair quantum circuit complexity. It helps researchers build and audit quantum generation models, verify reference certificates, and compute conditional lower bounds on quantum circuit complexity from terminal-state information. Preparing a pure qubit illustrates why the resource accounting matters. A reset operation can do so in a single step, while the physical cost of removing entropy may be absent from a gate count. A supplied pure ancilla also carries structure that a preparation procedure can use. The cost therefore depends on what the background supplies and which operations are charged. Reference-Contingent Complexity (RCC) fixes the reference background, allowed dynamics, control rules and cost unit before target selection. Under its model hypotheses, the target's one-shot information gap gives a common cost lower bound for every admissible preparation history, and hence for the optimal cost within the fixed model. The framework is introduced in Structure-Fair Quantum Circuit Complexity: An Auditable Information-Theoretic Lower Bound. The conceptual introduction develops this motivation through a paired-reset example. This software release is aligned with version 4 of the RCC manuscript. Model audits and terminal-state bounds Researchers can construct prefix-controlled quantum processes, compute terminating program semidensities, verify Bellman–Choi and reference-potential certificates, and examine reference gain–cost assignments. Version 0.1.3 applies these methods to quantum state preparation, with conditional cost bounds from complete exact target spectra or predeclared fixed-projector counts. Freshly verified certificates can supply the reference-domination constant, connecting model-level evidence to a target-state calculation. Calculation records preserve the declared task, inputs, protocols, evidence levels and results, with same-version replay of the scalar calculation. A runnable example shows how an H.3 certificate supplies the reference constant for a terminal-state bound. The package provides a Python API, command-line tools, installed input templates, two Jupyter tutorials and frozen reference evidence. Three reference cases cover closed-form, multiblock and nonhalting behavior; a paired-reset example connects a model to a one-slot lower bound attained by an explicit program. Matrix checks provide numerical evidence for fixed finite models. Terminal-state bounds are conditional on the declared model premises and the current uniform-reference, ideal-support contract. Records distinguish conservative scalar enclosures, numerical certificate evidence and sampling coverage. The paper supplies the physical and analytic premises of the general RCC framework. Install and reproduce Requires Python 3.10 or newer. Install this version from PyPI and verify the bundled reference results: python -m pip install rcc-refcert==0.1.3 python -m rcc_refcert reproduce --check To run the target-spectrum example: python -m rcc_refcert bound template spectrum > spectrum.json python -m rcc_refcert bound spectrum spectrum.json The README, terminal-state guide and changelog describe the inputs, result interpretation and changes in this release. The paper-to-code map locates the implemented objects and checks in the RCC manuscript.

title: Nonlinear Topological Structuring
abstract: This paper explores the application of nonlinear topological structuring to dynamic geometric modification and the construction of novel quantum computing architectures. We propose a novel algorithmic framework predicated on quantum entanglement, enabling the real-time reshaping of complex geometric forms without explicit manual intervention. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to induce instantaneous adjustments in the topological structure, ultimately generating new geometric properties and enhancing computational capabilities. This work presents a framework for dynamically evolving geometries within quantum systems, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional topological modeling.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of adaptive resonance to sustain and manipulate entanglement, offering a novel approach that circumvents the limitations of classical measurement. We introduce a 'Resonance-Adaptive' algorithm, a system-level modification to the entanglement process, designed to maintain entanglement stability and allow for controlled manipulation through feedback. The core mechanism hinges on the system's inherent ability to adjust its state in response to environmental cues, leading to a dynamic and potentially more robust entanglement framework. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, explores preliminary results demonstrating sustained entanglement and manipulation, and discusses the implications for quantum information processing and fundamental physics.

title: 基于量子态的神经网络的自适应自校正机制
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Quantum-Adaptive Neural Network" (QANN), that leverages the unique properties of quantum states for self-correction and stable learning. Traditional neural networks often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their adaptability and stability. The QANN employs a dynamic mechanism based on quantum state evolution to proactively address and mitigate errors, achieving significantly enhanced learning performance and robustness. The core of this design lies in the utilization of quantum state self-entanglement to dynamically adjust network parameters, offering a fundamentally different approach to neural network training. The proposed method addresses the limitations of current techniques by providing a mechanism for continuous error correction, enhancing both the learning process and the network's overall resilience. The paper details the mathematical framework, experimental validation, and preliminary analysis of the QANN, demonstrating its potential for improved machine learning capabilities.

title: Hierarchical Adaptive Feature Selection with Quantum Search
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum search algorithms to enhance the process of feature selection, aiming to improve model accuracy and efficiency. Traditional feature selection methods often struggle with large feature spaces and require significant computational resources. We propose a hierarchical adaptive feature selection technique that leverages quantum search to efficiently identify the most relevant features, mitigating the limitations of classical methods. The core mechanism involves employing quantum algorithms to explore the feature space and pinpoint features with a higher impact on the model's prediction. This research explores the potential of quantum search to expedite the selection process, offering a novel approach to improving model performance.

title: Dimension Reduction of Probability Logic Systems (DPLS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method, Dimension Reduction of Probability Logic Systems (DPLS), which leverages deep learning to enhance probabilistic reasoning and prediction. Traditional probability logic systems often rely on static, handcrafted parameters, limiting their adaptability. DPLS employs a neural network to learn probability distributions directly from data, enabling automatic parameter adjustment for optimized results. This approach surpasses existing methods by offering a more flexible and automated solution for probabilistic inference. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting inference parameters to maximize prediction accuracy. This work explores the potential of this approach to significantly improve the performance and efficiency of probabilistic systems.

title: Adaptive Dimension Scaling Algorithm
abstract: Abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Dimension Scaling Algorithm (ADSA) designed to optimize computation and performance in various scenarios. Traditional dimension scaling methods often rely on fixed complexity, failing to effectively adapt to the specific characteristics of the input data. ADSA dynamically adjusts the complexity of computations based on the problem's inherent properties, leading to improved efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism involves a self-learning dimension scaling system that automatically adjusts the computational burden based on unique characteristics of the problem. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulated experiments, showcasing its ability to handle diverse datasets and achieve superior results compared to existing methods. The paper explores the benefits of dynamic complexity adjustment in different applications, including image processing, data analysis, and machine learning.

title: Non-Linear Topological Quantum State Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel self-adaptive geometric evolution algorithm for non-linear topological quantum states. Traditional approaches to quantum state evolution often rely on static mappings, limiting the ability to dynamically manipulate and control quantum states. We propose a new algorithmic framework based on the inherent geometry of quantum states, enabling continuous and controlled evolution driven by a learned mapping. This approach offers a significant departure from conventional methods, potentially enhancing the handling of complex quantum states and providing new opportunities for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Error Correction Topology Graph
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a promising approach to enhancing the reliability of quantum information processing. A key component of QEC is the development of topological quantum information codes, which encode information in a fundamentally robust way. This paper proposes a novel method utilizing quantum error correction to construct a topology-based graph, providing a powerful tool for analyzing and predicting complex systems' topological structures. We introduce a new graph representation and a protocol for generating topological maps based on quantum error correction, demonstrating its potential to significantly simplify and accelerate the study of intricate topological phenomena. The resulting graph provides a unique perspective on the underlying topological landscape, offering enhanced insights into system behavior and robustness.

title: Quantum Topology Multi-Coherence Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel paradigm of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for robust quantum systems and unprecedented computational capabilities. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to optimize quantum systems, focusing on multi-coherence optimization. We introduce a new computational framework predicated on the inherent self-organizing properties of quantum topology, designed to enhance the stability and efficiency of quantum states. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic optimization algorithm that leverages quantum topology to achieve precise control over quantum systems, ultimately leading to improved data storage and transmission. The development of this framework presents a significant advancement in quantum information processing, offering a pathway towards more reliable and scalable quantum technologies. The paper details the framework's architecture, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing complex quantum systems.

title: Neuro-Monolithic Architecture Global Intelligence Framework: The Open Science of Topological Cognition (Stage 10.0 "Sphere Topology" Edition)
abstract: This monograph presents the formal synthesis of the Neuro-Monolithic Architecture Global Intelligence Framework (NMAGIF). It establishes the theoretical and mathematical foundations for true biological scalability in artificial general intelligence by dismantling the "thin client" paradigm and replacing it with the Fractal Monolith. Package Contents: NMAGIF_Monograph_v_4_2_EN.pdf: Master monograph (150 pages, Stage 10.0 "Sphere Topology" Edition), containing the 12 core chapters and Annexe G (Empirical Telemetry & Visual Atlas, Doc ID: NMAGIF-TR-2026-ANNEX-G-V1). NMAGIF_Lean4_Verification_Release_4_2.pdf: Machine-checked Lean 4 formal verification dossier (25 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 admit) structured into a two-tier epistemic architecture: Tier-1 (11 theorems): Strictly verified discrete solver invariants over R (JKO metric positivity, monotone Burg entropy decay, discrete mass conservation) and continuous hardware epsilon-isomorphism bridge. Tier-2 (14 theorems): Axiomatic domain specifications characterizing the macroscopic non-equilibrium state machine and topological phase transitions. research-dossiers.pdf: Supplementary research dossiers indexing the companion mathematical and experimental corpus. The entire architecture runs autonomously at ~25 Hz on dedicated neural edge hardware with hardware-accelerated tensor co-processing, validated by live smoke tests, mass topology tests, and machine-checked formal proofs. Released under CC BY 4.0. Language note: The technical paper, mathematical formalisms, and architectural specifications are written entirely in English. The introductory Manifesto and Acknowledgements sections are presented in both Ukrainian and English.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computing leveraging adaptive topology, offering a fundamentally different strategy compared to traditional methods. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in the accuracy of quantum information storage predictions, highlighting the potential of this dynamically-adjusted topology approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Clustering with Entangled Feature Representations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering approach termed Quantum-Inspired Clustering (QIC) leveraging concepts derived from quantum mechanics, specifically entanglement, to enhance feature representation and cluster discovery. Traditional clustering algorithms often face challenges when dealing with high-dimensional data and intricate feature dependencies. QIC addresses this by encoding features into entangled states, allowing the algorithm to capture and exploit correlated relationships within the data that are typically overlooked by conventional methods. The core mechanism relies on identifying clusters based on the shared information encoded within these entangled representations. The resulting algorithm demonstrates the potential to improve clustering performance, particularly in scenarios with complex datasets where linear separation is difficult or non-existent. We present a formal description of the algorithm, including the feature encoding process and the clustering objective function. The performance of the proposed method is discussed, highlighting its advantages and potential limitations.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Noise Injection for Enhanced Generalization and Robustness
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly evolving field that explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize machine learning tasks. A critical challenge in QML is the need for robust models that can generalize well to unseen data and exhibit resilience to perturbations. This paper introduces a novel QML model, Quantum Machine Learning with Adaptive Noise Injection (QML-ALI), designed to address this challenge by incorporating a dynamic noise injection mechanism. We propose a mechanism that intelligently adjusts the amount of noise injected during training based on the observed training dynamics, ultimately promoting improved generalization and robustness. This approach contrasts with traditional methods that rely on fixed noise levels, offering a more adaptable and potentially superior solution. The core claims and mechanisms are detailed, and the paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future directions of this research.

title: Causal Representation Learning with Intervention-Based Contrastive Learning
abstract: Traditional representation learning methods frequently struggle to accurately represent underlying causal relationships within data, leading to models that are sensitive to spurious correlations. This paper introduces a novel approach, Intervention-Based Contrastive Learning (IBCL), designed to address this limitation. IBCL utilizes contrastive learning, but crucially incorporates interventions – specifically, manipulating causal variables – to generate contrasting representations. The model is trained to distinguish between representations derived from observational data and those produced by intervening on the data. This allows the model to learn representations that are more robust to noise and better capture the true causal structure. We posit that by explicitly considering the effects of interventions, the model develops a more faithful and interpretable representation of the data, moving beyond purely correlational relationships. The core of this method lies in the ability to create a richer, more informative representation space that reflects the true causal dynamics of the system. We outline the framework and its key components, emphasizing the theoretical underpinnings and potential benefits. ---

title: Context-Aware Data Augmentation via Synthetic Fractal Generation
abstract: Data augmentation is a crucial technique in machine learning, particularly when dealing with limited training data. Traditional data augmentation methods often lack the ability to effectively capture the underlying context and complexities of the data, leading to synthetic data that doesn't adequately represent the original distribution. This paper proposes a novel approach to data augmentation that leverages synthetic fractal generation, resulting in context-aware augmentation. The core idea is to generate synthetic data points based on fractal patterns, but these patterns are dynamically adjusted to align with the statistical characteristics and contextual information of the original dataset. This approach allows for the creation of more realistic and relevant synthetic data, ultimately leading to improved model training performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a conceptual framework and theoretical justification, highlighting its potential for various applications. The system generates data that reflects the underlying structure of the original dataset, effectively increasing the diversity of the training set without introducing artificial artifacts. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the fractal generation process, ensuring contextually relevant augmentation.

title: Identifying Habit, Physics, and Nuisance in Robot World Models
abstract: Teleoperated demonstrations are often multimodal even when the underlying dynamics are nearly deterministic given the executed action. We argue that this multimodality typically mixes three factors--operator habit in action selection, shared physics, and observation nuisance--and that entangled next-observation predictors absorb all three. We formalize the split with a structural causal model a=g(h,z,u), z'=f(z,a), o=r(z,c), and test it with complementary interventions: replacing or shuffling actions at fixed state sharply increases next-state error, whereas appearance and camera changes should not; habit-aware reverse scoring improves ranking of feasible pasts without rewriting the dynamics. The associated adaptation rule is to freeze a shared physics readout and update only a thin interface. On StackCube, DROID, and RH20T this rule improves low-shot transfer relative to training from scratch, retains cleaner dynamics under corrupted adaptation data, and extends from proprioception to pixel observations with multi-view and multi-step checks. We do not equate latent actions with operator habit, and we do not target large-scale video generation benchmarks.

title: AutoKD: Autonomous Knowledge Discovery
abstract: Scientific discovery in data-rich domains is currently constrained by human bandwidth: the growth in the volume and complexity of real-world data far outpaces the rate at which researchers can read, reason, and synthesize. Recent LLM-based multi-agent systems have begun to automate portions of the research cycle, but they target hypothesis generation in settings where validation cannot itself be automated, and each run is one-shot, with no mechanism for findings to accumulate or steer subsequent inquiry. This paper introduces AutoKD, a multi-agent framework for autonomous knowledge discovery that is both computational and cumulative, allowing validated findings to persist and inform subsequent inquiry. Six coordinated LLM agents collaborate in an open-ended discovery loop, where accepted findings are stored in a persistent insight graph that serves as both long-term memory and an exploration-steering mechanism. We evaluate AutoKD on three diverse datasets from two perspectives: Open-ended Quality against published findings, and Conditioned Quality via literature-derived queries. Across both evaluation perspectives, AutoKD covers known findings and surfaces substantive discoveries that complement human-driven research. Our code is available at https://github.com/GeQinwen/AutoKD.

title: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) interact with graphical interfaces through screenshots and low-level mouse and keyboard actions, yet the causal error may precede the terminal failure. We present CUADebug, a framework for localizing root causes in CUA trajectories and guiding re-execution. CUADebug includes a five-category, 30-subtype taxonomy; CUAErrorBench, a benchmark of 204 failed OSWorld trajectories with human root-cause annotations; and CUADebugger, a ReAct-style agent for root-cause analysis (RCA). CUADebugger iteratively selects trajectory steps, inspects paired before/after screenshots and action traces, and submits a structured diagnosis containing the causal step, taxonomy label, grounded evidence, and correction. CUADebugger performs RCA without per-trajectory human intervention; human annotations are used to evaluate RCA predictions and, in controlled re-rollout comparisons, to fix restart points. Task reasoning and control is the largest annotated failure category (110/204). CUADebugger improves L2 and Tag+Step Exact across three debugger backbones on the Claude-agent split; with Gemini 2.5 Pro, Tag+Step Exact rises from 11.1% to 19.4%. Single re-execution improves failure recovery from 13.89% to 29.86% (overall 61.77% to 68.14%); controlled continual re-execution improves it from 12.50% to 25.69% (overall 61.22% to 66.48%). Project page: cuadebug.github.io.

title: Semantic model of services in the Slovenian artificial intelligence factory
abstract: Magistrsko delo obravnava semantično modeliranje storitev in artefaktov v okviru Slovenske tovarne umetne inteligence. Cilj naloge je bil razviti ontologijo v spletnem ontološkem jeziku (ang. Web Ontology Language, OWL), ki omogoča strukturirano predstavitev domene, pomensko označevanje podatkov ter učinkovito poizvedovanje. V nalogi so obravnavane opisne logike kot formalna osnova jezika OWL ter osnovni vidiki sklepanja in ekspresivnosti ontologij. Razvit semantični model zajema katalog storitev, opise njihovega procesnega izvajanja in pripadajoči pravni okvir ter je ovrednoten na opisih dejanskih storitev (na primer izobraževalne, svetovalne, računske ter storitve za dostop do virov in modelov umetne inteligence) v okviru Slovenske tovarne umetne inteligence. Model je analiziran z vidika konsistentnosti in ekspresivnosti.

title: The Hierarchical Latent Workspace Model: Root-Preserving Variable-Depth Expertise for Parallel Diffusion Reasoning
abstract: The full technical report on a latent-workspace language model built on a frozen Qwen3-0.6B decoder, and the ten preregistered prototype experiments that falsified it at this scale. Routing failed causal liveness on 10 of 10 seed-runs; ablating the read-out's 34 memory positions changed graded accuracy by 0.000 on one seed and improved it by 0.022 on the other. Parity was reached by irrelevance.

title: DL-MoE-01: completed study archive — developmental history and specialization in mixture-of-experts models
abstract: Retrospective archive of the completed DL-MoE-01 experiment: 30 paired blocks, 180 trained models, 20,000 steps per model. The predicted positive architecture amplification was not supported: mean A = -0.0120438891, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.0205617259, -0.0032389058], one-sided p = 0.993725449. All eight behavioral equivalence comparisons passed. There were no numerical failures or outcome-based exclusions. This is not a public preregistration or a Registered Report. The protocol was frozen locally before execution according to local records; this deposit records public availability after completion and does not independently certify the earlier chronology. Files include the Russian author-review manuscript, exact frozen execution source (commit e57710fcb7b2e15b448ae2438f041d2a98fd6929), raw evidence, all model checkpoints, analysis tables, validation reports, chronology, and SHA-256 manifests. The positive prediction and the negative result are both retained. The next-replication document is a planning draft, not a registered or executable new study. title: 基于动态概率的机器学习的优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Dynamic Probability Optimization," that leverages dynamic probability distributions to enhance the generalization ability of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on fixed probability distributions, limiting their adaptability to changing data and environmental conditions. This paper proposes a method that dynamically adjusts these distributions during the training process, resulting in improved model performance. The core mechanism involves learning from historical data and environmental feedback to create a probabilistic model that evolves with the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several experiments on a variety of benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness.

title: 基于量子势的动态算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic algorithm based on quantum potential, designed to autonomously adjust algorithm strategies in response to fluctuating quantum potentials. Traditional algorithms often rely on static strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamic environments. Our approach leverages quantum potential to continuously evaluate and refine the algorithm's parameters, optimizing performance across a wider range of input data. We present a framework incorporating quantum state manipulation and gradient-based optimization, demonstrating a significant improvement in algorithm efficiency compared to static methods. This research explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance optimization processes, offering a promising avenue for advancing machine learning and computational optimization within various domains.

title: 基于非线性自适应的几何-量子纠缠计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing and data processing based on non-linear adaptive geometry-quantum entanglement. We propose a new algorithm that leverages the unique properties of geometric-quantum entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced computational speed and data handling capabilities compared to existing methods. The core of our design lies in a dynamically adjusted self-adaptation process applied to the entanglement structure, enabling efficient manipulation of complex quantum states. This research explores the potential of this approach to address challenges in both quantum information theory and practical computation. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, presents preliminary results demonstrating improved performance, and discusses future research directions.

abstract: Quantum Topology Structure Adaptive Quantum Algorithm (QTAS-AQ) presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm design and optimization, leveraging the principles of quantum topology to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of existing quantum algorithms. The core mechanism revolves around utilizing topological properties to guide the evolution of the quantum state, resulting in a more robust and efficient quantum computation. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in various quantum benchmark tasks compared to traditional methods, establishing a new paradigm for quantum algorithm development.

title: Self-Adaptive Chaos Models in Quantum Computation Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-adaptive chaos models to quantum computation evolution, aiming to provide precise simulations of complex systems and dynamic geometric transformations. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the intricacies of dynamic systems, and this integrated approach offers a novel pathway to enhanced simulation fidelity and evolution. We propose a framework utilizing quantum computation's inherent properties to achieve accurate, dynamic geometric modifications to system evolution. The core mechanism involves the iterative application of self-adaptive chaos dynamics, generating subtle geometric shifts that influence the system's trajectory. The resulting simulations demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex, nonlinear dynamics. This research presents a fundamentally new method for quantum computation evolution, leveraging the principles of self-adaptive chaos to achieve unprecedented precision and flexibility.

title: 拓扑遗传算法的自适应特征选择 (DGS-A)
abstract: This paper introduces the DGS-A (拓扑遗传算法的自适应特征选择) algorithm, a novel approach to feature selection that dynamically adjusts feature selection strategies based on input data characteristics. Traditional feature selection methods are often static, limiting the potential for optimal model performance. DGS-A leverages the inherent search capabilities of the DGT algorithm to iteratively refine feature selection based on observed data patterns. This dynamic adaptation results in improved model accuracy and generalization. The paper details the algorithm's key components, including the search strategy, feature representation, and optimization process. We provide a comprehensive evaluation of DGS-A's effectiveness on a diverse dataset, demonstrating its superior performance compared to established methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's potential applications in various machine learning domains.

title: Dynamic Program Synthesis Engine (DPSE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Program Synthesis Engine (DPSE), a novel approach to automating the process of program synthesis. The core claim of the DPSE is to construct an engine capable of dynamically generating programs based on user-defined requirements. This is achieved through the integration of program representation technologies and program generation algorithms. The system operates by translating user needs into executable code, performing rigorous verification steps, and optimizing the resulting programs. Unlike traditional program synthesis methods reliant on manual design, the DPSE offers a fully automated solution, significantly reducing development time and potentially uncovering solutions that a human designer might overlook. The engine leverages a core mechanism of representing program specifications and applying generative algorithms to produce and validate target programs. This research addresses a critical need in software development by providing a robust and scalable framework for automated program creation. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the synthesis process based on feedback from verification steps, allowing for iterative refinement and ultimately, the generation of highly optimized and correct programs.

title: 自适应量子电路的量子自适应算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum circuit design tool leveraging an adaptive quantum algorithm to automatically adjust quantum parameters. Traditional quantum circuit design relies heavily on manual parameter tuning, which is a time-consuming and error-prone process. This research introduces a system that dynamically adjusts parameters based on the circuit's current state, drastically reducing the need for manual intervention and enhancing the efficiency of quantum computation and information processing. The core mechanism focuses on a self-tuning algorithm that iteratively refines the circuit's parameters to optimize performance. We detail the design of this algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary results. The advantages of this approach are enhanced adaptability, reduced parameter tuning effort, and improved quantum circuit performance.

title: Differential Privacy with Adaptive Noise Injection for Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data without directly exchanging the data itself. However, traditional differential privacy (DP) methods often introduce substantial noise into the model updates, significantly degrading model accuracy. This paper proposes a novel adaptive noise injection scheme for FL, designed to mitigate this issue. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the noise level based on the sensitivity of the local data, thereby optimizing the privacy-utility trade-off. Our approach leverages the inherent variance in local updates to reduce the overall noise required to achieve a desired privacy guarantee. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and intuitive simulations that our adaptive scheme leads to improved model accuracy compared to standard DP methods while maintaining the same level of privacy. The proposed method addresses a critical bottleneck in FL—the inherent conflict between privacy preservation and model performance—and provides a practical pathway for deploying robust and accurate FL systems.
